# Andreas Kapsner — "Cutting Corners: A Critical Note on Priest's Five-Valued Catuṣkoṭi" (2020)

## Bibliographic identity

The selected object is Andreas Kapsner, "Cutting Corners: A Critical Note on Priest's Five-Valued Catuṣkoṭi," *Comparative Philosophy* 11, no. 2 (2020), open access at scholarworks.sjsu.edu. Metadata and abstract verified against the journal record; the full text is freely available but has not yet been extracted into this house, so only the abstract is currently quotation-ready. Article page range to be fixed at extraction.

## Chicago 18 forms

**Shortened note:** Kapsner, "Cutting Corners."

**Bibliography:** Kapsner, Andreas. "Cutting Corners: A Critical Note on Priest's Five-Valued Catuṣkoṭi." *Comparative Philosophy* 11, no. 2 (2020).

## Source scholarship

Kapsner writes from inside the non-classical camp — a logician friendly to Priest's general program — and aims his critical note at one component only: the fifth value. Per the verified abstract, the note "examines that fifth value and raises some concerns about it that seem grave enough to reject it. It then sketches an alternative to Priest's account that has no need for the fifth value." The shape of the objection matters more to the essay than its detail: the four-valued FDE reading of the corners is left standing, and what falls is precisely the promotion of ineffability to a *value* — a fifth thing of the same kind as the four. Even a sympathetic reconstruction, Kapsner shows, can keep everything Priest wants from the catuṣkoṭi while refusing to reify "none of the above" into a semantic status. Full-text extraction will supply the concerns themselves (their grounds and the sketched alternative); until then this house carries the abstract's exact wording and the article's role.

## Essay use

### Source's relevant contribution

The gate-source: the friendliest available logician's objection to Priest, targeting exactly the fifth value.

### Licensed essay use

- Cite in [[28-s3-p3-projective-dimensional-reframing]] as the sharpest internal objection to the five-valued construction, alongside the reception gates in [[symbolon/episteme/sources/mathematics-logic/priest/priest-2018-fifth-corner/priest-2018-fifth-corner.md|priest-2018-fifth-corner]].
- Use the objection's shape to display QL's difference: Kapsner rejects ineffability *as a value*; QL's ground-position #0 is not a truth-value at all but a generative precondition, so the objection does not reach it. Citing Kapsner shows the essay knows the construction's weak joint and does not stand on it.

### Claim boundary

Kapsner does not know or discuss QL; the claim that his objection leaves QL's #0 untouched is the essay's own Argued move. Until full-text extraction, no wording beyond the abstract may be quoted, and the content of his "grave concerns" may be characterized only at abstract level.
